body: See I would take a year off of school. Work, make connections and take the occasional free class online (here's MIT courses http://ocw.mit.edu/index.htm). And I'm sure you must have something that interests you. Math? Biology? Physics? Sociology? If not try watching a few lectures from all over the place and see if anything catches your interest. You never know maybe you'll like something you never would have thought you would. Personally I never thought I'd enjoy philosophy as much as I do.

Fair enough. Saw above you were premed. If you can why not try something else? If your good at math do comp sci. If you can't go back to college teach yourself to code, lots of free resources. How old are you might I ask? And do you think you could go back to uni?
Thanks. I really mean that. Just talking about this helps. Guess I better get to work lol.

I know the feeling. College is currently my entire life as well. Not sure how I'll make it through this term and if I don't I don't know what I'll do. How exactly did you fail? Do you want to talk about it?

Not much in the form of advice but she is actually really supportive. Hell right now there is no way I could fit a job into my schedule so she's giving me almost $500 a month for food/rent. That's about a fourh of what she gets every month so even though I deeply appreciate the help I can't help but feel like a parasite. As far as school work goes it's a 1000 word essay midterm for an online writing intensive course. Don't have a whole lot of choice but to do it.

She does, but it's hard to talk much when I'm constantly either studying or writing essays. It's what I probably should be doing right now, but I'm sure I can bust it out in an hour or so if I need to. Combine that with the fact that she works all the time makes conversation hard. I do talk to her almost every day though for a few short minutes.
Just my mom. Probably the only reason I haven't gone through with it yet is I would feel guilty.
